rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative for a forward cluster with 11:19 addresses only sowing/reaping vocabulary and omits the verse's actual shared exact token with 11:19.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived by token-splitting each verse's skeleton and checking for an EXACT (not merely contiguous-substring) match: oshb:Prov.11.18 and oshb:Prov.11.19 both carry the bare, word-bound, unprefixed token צדקה -- confirmed, not a prefixed variant. CORRECT OBJECT + DIGIT for this claim: exact word-bound skeleton token צדקה (unprefixed) -> 10 verses book-wide (Prov.8.20, 11.18, 11.19, 12.28, 13.6, 14.34, 15.9, 16.31, 21.3, 21.21), with 11:18-11:19 the SOLE adjacent pair -- LF's digit, independently reproduced exactly and correctly scoped (see P05-052 rulings for the full digit reconciliation against OL's 15-count). This matches the same rarity/single-adjacent-pair profile the writer itself used to justify the P05-058 proverb_cluster ruling for ברכה (3 verses book-wide, one adjacent pair; independently reproduced, sweep.py --skel). The row's rejected_alternative tests 11:19 only against 11:18's sowing/reaping IMAGERY and never engages the shared noun, so the rival candidate is not rejected on its actual strongest evidence.
rulings.remedy: ONE work order shared with the P05-052 rulings below (do not open a second ticket for the same 11:18|11:19 boundary defect): rewrite P05-051's and P05-052's rejected_alternative/rationale fields to name the shared exact token צדקה (word-bound, unprefixed, 10 verses book-wide, sole adjacent pair) instead of denying shared wording, then re-argue why single_proverb still holds (e.g., 11:19 as a synthetic conclusion-clause drawing an inference from 11:18, rather than an independent topic) -- or flip to proverb_cluster if the boss round finds the shared-noun evidence controlling. Test the cure must pass: collate.py + sweep.py --skel re-run against the revised prose must show no remaining claim of absent shared wording.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row explicitly and falsely claims 11:18 and 11:19 "share no repeated wording," undercounts the cross-referenced occurrences of its cited noun, and its own quotes are unlabeled skeleton tier.
rulings.grounds: SAME CORE DEFECT as the LF/P05-052 ruling above -- both primaries independently found the identical false "no shared wording" claim; ONE convergent defect, not two. DIGIT RECONCILIATION (resolving the object first, per assignment directive): OL's cited "15 verses book-wide" is REPRODUCED EXACTLY by me via sweep.py --skel "צדקה" -- but that tool call is a documented CONTIGUOUS CONSONANTAL SUBSTRING search (sweep.py's own docstring: "not a root/lemma search"), which also catches the noun's PREFIXED forms (5 extra verses: Prov.8.18, 10.2, 11.4, 16.8, 16.12, independently confirmed by token-level check to carry prefixed variants, not the bare token). OL's prose labels this digit "the exact skeleton token," which mis-names what the digit actually measures -- OL BLENDED two distinct objects (exact token vs. prefix-inclusive substring) under one label, contrary to the toolkit's SEMANTIC-CLASS COUNT DISCIPLINE ("name the swept object FIRST... blended sweeps forbidden"). CORRECTED FINDING: the properly-scoped object+digit for this claim is the word-bound exact token צדקה -> 10 verses (LF's citation, ruling above), not 15. This does NOT weaken OL's core charge -- the row's "no repeated wording" claim is false under either object definition, since 11:18/11:19 both carry the token under the NARROWER, correct definition too. The לחיים undercount (4 vs. the row's implied 2) and the unlabeled-skeleton-tier point are independently confirmed accurate as stated.
rulings.remedy: Same single work order as the LF/P05-052 ruling above -- do not open a second ticket. When re-citing the shared-token evidence in any revised packet, use the word-bound exact-token digit (10) with the object named explicitly ("exact token צדקה, unprefixed"), not the raw sweep.py --skel substring digit (15) mislabeled as exact.
